summary: Minimal, correct fix: replacing the hand-rolled AttributeError with a re-call to self.__getattribute__(attr) lets a nested AttributeError (e.g. from a subclass property accessing a missing attribute) propagate with the correct attribute name, while the normal missing-attribute path still produces the standard Python message. This is the well-known idiom and introduces no recursion or message-format regression.

issues.description: On the error path __getattribute__ re-runs full attribute lookup, so any property getter is invoked a second time; side-effecting getters would execute twice. Only affects the failure path, negligible in practice.

Comment 'this will give correct exception' is terse; a brief note explaining that an explicit __getattribute__ call does not re-trigger __getattr__ (hence no recursion) and surfaces the original nested AttributeError would aid future maintainers.
